title: Efficacy and safety of oral semaglutide 14 mg (flexible dose) in early-stage symptomatic Alzheimer's disease (evoke and evoke+): two phase 3, randomised, placebo-controlled trials
authors: Cummings JL, Atri A, Sano M, Zetterberg H, Scheltens P, Knop FK, et al.
followUp: primary end point at week 104; planned treatment up to 156 weeks; both trials discontinued for a negative clinical outcome
population: Adults aged 55 to 85 with amyloid-confirmed mild cognitive impairment or mild dementia due to Alzheimer's disease at 566 sites in 40 countries; mean age 72.2 years
funder: Funding: Novo Nordisk, as stated in the abstract; four authors are Novo Nordisk employees and minor shareholders.
result: Change in Clinical Dementia Rating-Sum of Boxes from baseline to week 104 was 2.3 on semaglutide against 2.3 on placebo in evoke (difference -0.08, 95% CI -0.35 to 0.20) and 2.2 against 2.1 in evoke+ (0.10, -0.17 to 0.38). Treatment-emergent adverse events in 1729 of 1896 (91.2%) against 1613 of 1902 (84.8%). The trials were motivated by animal, clinical and observational findings of lower dementia risk after GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure.
